title: Consumer-facing endpoint contracts PRD and launch QA playbook
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: This ticket is the Product Requirements Document (PRD) and accompanying QA playbook for the consumer-facing behavior contracts of the hosted inference surface covering chat, completions, embeddings and rerank endpoints. Focus is on precise behavioral contracts, measurable acceptance criteria, rollout guardrails, and a deterministic QA plan for launch.
background: Multiple recent incidents highlighted ambiguity in endpoint behavior when model variants, tokenization differences, and structured output options are combined. Teams require a single consumer contract document that ties API shape to latency/cost SLOs, quality evaluations, and rollout procedures to avoid regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
goals: Define a deterministic behavioral contract for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints
Quantify latency and cost SLOs and regression thresholds
Provide a QA playbook with traffic slices, eval datasets and canary criteria
Ensure SDKs/docs and migration guidance are ready at launch
scope_in: API request/response schemas for chat and completion
Embeddings vector dimension and normalization rules
Rerank API scoring semantics and tie-breakers
Canary and gradual rollouts for hosted lanes
scope_out: Model training or changes to model architectures
On-prem installation guides for Private deployment (separate project)
Large-scale privacy audits beyond standard KMS integration
acceptance_criteria: API schema docs published and verified in Console (routes + examples)
All contract tests pass for 3 representative model families (decoder-only, seq2seq, instruction-tuned) on staging within 2 weeks of PR approval
Latency: p50 <= 60ms and p95 <= 200ms for text-completions baseline profile on hosted-small lane with standard 1k token context within accepted variance (+/-10%)
Embeddings: cosine similarity stable within +/-0.03 on canonical evaluation sets after quantization/transport
Rerank: NDCG@10 regression <= 1.5% vs baseline on benchmark sets
Function-calling structured output: 95% parse success rate for approved function schemas in test harness
Canary criteria: 10% traffic ramp for 48 hours with no increase in error budget or critical user-facing bugs
SDKs for Python and Typescript updated and integration smoke tests pass
Docs, migration guide, and example apps published and linked from Console
Operational runbook and rollback plan attached to the release and validated in a tabletop exercise
launch_checklist: Finalize PRD and get sign-off from Eng, Design, Security and Support
Create contract test suite in CI with synthetic and recorded traffic
Run eval harness across 5 curated prompt sets for each endpoint; capture metrics
Deploy canary configuration in hosted-staging and validate telemetry collection
Execute tabletop rollback and incident playbook with on-call rotation
Publish SDK changes and coordinate minor versions with downstream integrators
Add telemetry dashboards for cost-per-token, latency percentiles, and quality regressions
Enable gradual rollout gates (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers
Announce changelog and migration notes to internal docs and external changelog
decisions: Normalize embeddings to L2 unit vectors at SDK layer to reduce downstream variance
Expose a 'model_variant' header for deterministic routing and observability
Default function-calling to strict schema parsing in hosted lane; lenient in beta lane
Quantization profiles will be opt-in per model and documented with expected quality delta
open_questions: What is the acceptable tokenization mismatch tolerance between models that share an endpoint?
Do we enforce a single canonical embedding dimension across all hosted models or allow per-model dims with runtime conversion?
Should rerank return raw scores or normalized probabilities by default?
What SLA tiers (bronze/silver/gold) should map to which latency/throughput guarantees?

notes: This PRD emphasizes measurable acceptance and a conservative rollout. The QA playbook intentionally prioritizes safety gates over feature breadth for initial launch; additional features will be staged in follow-up epics.
